title: Adaptive Utility Optimization for Stochastic Renewal Systems
summary: This paper treats a system that performs back-to-back tasks. Each new task has a random matrix of parameters and can be processed in various processing modes. The processing mode determines the task duration and a vector of rewards (penalties are viewed as negative rewards). The reward vector can include quality, profit, or $-1$ times a penalty such as cost or energy. In wireless applications, tasks correspond to data transmissions and rewards/penalties correspond to throughput and distortion.
